# Other Problems Concerning the Spleen Follow.

There is the question why the <term>spleen</term> <note>original: "Milz"</note>, as far as its substance and essence are concerned, is a black flesh? And furthermore, why is it so? Firstly, according to the opinion of <term>Aristotle</term>, the spleen is made of earthly and black matter, and its <term>effect</term> <note>original: "Effectus"</note> becomes like its <term>cause</term> <note>original: "Causa"</note>; "the effect testifies to the cause," <note>original Latin: "Effectus testatur de causa"</note> as one is accustomed to say in this regard. Besides this, one also usually answers along with the <term>physicians</term> <note>original: "Medicis"</note> that the spleen is a <term>receptacle</term> <note>original: "Receptaculum"</note>, chamber, or vessel for <term>melancholy</term> <note>original: "Melancholiae"</note>. <term>Melancholy</term> <note>original: "Melancholia"</note>, however, is a black <term>humor</term> <note>one of the four vital bodily fluids in ancient medicine</note>, and by its nature, it is similarly not directed toward any wasteland <note>original: "keiner öde Verrecht"; likely meaning this substance is not without its specific purpose</note>. For <term>melancholy</term>, according to its <term>etymology</term>, is the same as black <term>bile</term> <note>original: "schwartze Cholera"</note>. Item: Why are people who have a large spleen dry and haggard, as <term>Aristotle</term> says, and as is also to be seen in <term>melancholic</term> people? To this it is answered: the spleen draws much dry matter to itself, which should have been transformed into fat and become flesh.

# Glass of Venus or Copper-glass
->is made thus.<-

Take 2 parts: <term>Saturn</term> <note>original: "saturni"; the alchemical name for lead</note> or Lead, and 1 part: <term>Venus</term> <note>original: "Veneris"; the alchemical name for copper</note> or Copper, melt them together in a crucible. When they are properly melted, let them become cold; thereafter, take or lay them in a vessel with <term>nitric acid</term> <note>original: "Scheidwaßer"; literally "parting water," used to separate metals</note>, and set them overnight or even longer in a <term>reverberatory furnace</term> <note>original: "Reverberir Offen"; a furnace that reflects heat onto the material</note>. The vessel should stand over or upon another vessel; but you, see to it that the material boils upon it constantly and without ceasing. And what [sublimes] out from the first vessel above, that will be found lying on the other vessel; then let it become cold, and take it out, and see whether it be properly made <term>Glass of Venus</term> or Copper-glass or not. If it flows or melts quickly, then it is right; but if it does not melt soon, then repeat the <term>reverberation</term> <note>the process of heating in the furnace</note> until it flows or melts quickly. And let it not be brought less into the <term>body</term> <note>original: "Corpus"; the physical substance of the metal</note> than copper, but rather remain of a very red nature.

# Following is a Chapter on the Nature, Generation or Birth, the Figure, Kind, and Condition or State of All Metals in General

<margin>II To generate</margin>
All bodies that are contained and preserved under the high heaven where the sun runs, and are created by GOD the Almighty Creator, are made and composed of the Four Elements, and a portion comes from each element. From these come four natural **humors** <term>the four bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—thought to determine health</term> or moistures; from these, the four **complexions** <term>the temperament or nature of a substance (e.g., hot, cold, moist, or dry)</term>; from these, the four primary colors; from these, the four **flavors** <note>original: "Sapores"</note>; from these, the four **odors** <note>original: "Odoribus"</note>; and from these, the three **dimensions** <note>original: "Dimensionibus"</note> or measurements: that is, according to height, breadth, and thickness or depth. The four elements, however, are these:

<column-break/>

Fire, Air, Water, Earth. The four natural humors are these: **Cholera** <note>yellow bile</note>, **Sanguis** <note>blood</note>, **Phlegma** <note>phlegm</note>, and **Melancholia** <note>black bile</note>. The four natural complexions are: Heat or warmth, Moisture, Cold, and Dryness. The four primary colors are: White, Black, Yellow, and Red. The four flavors or tastes are: Sweet taste, Sour, Sweet <note>the original text repeats "Sweet" (Süße) here</note>, and Tart or Bitter. The four odors or smells are: Pleasant-smelling, Stinking, Sharp, and that which gives off no smell or only a very slight one. The three **sexes** <note>original: "Sexus"</note> or genders, however, are: Male and Female together <note>likely referring to the androgynous or hermaphroditic nature of certain alchemical substances</note>. The common height is a *manifestum*, which is its outward appearance; the Depth is its secret or hidden aspect; and the Breadth is called the mouth, the *medium* <note>the middle</note> or that same part. Therefore, in all bodies, according to all three dimensions, one must consider and contemplate all that has been well-mentioned. Just as a body in its height is **earthly** <term>Latin: *terrenum*; belonging to the element of earth</term>, so it is above: something cold, dry, melancholic, [slimy], stinking, and feminine. And the stomach follows, which in its depth is something airy, warm, and moist, yellowish, semi-sweet, and upright-smelling.

<meta>This page continues the technical discussion of the composition of metals. ### Therefore, it follows.

For indeed, the perfect and imperfect **bodies** <term>in alchemy, "bodies" refers to the solid metals</term> share the same matter, which may only be distinguished from one another in their **accidents** <term>outward or non-essential qualities, like color or hardness</term> or by chance circumstances. According to the opinion of all philosophers, this universal matter is **quicksilver** <note>original: "Argentum Vivum", literally "living silver"</note>, which Nature and the Earth have thoroughly cooked by the heat of sulfur in the womb of the earth. Aristotle is also of this opinion at the end of the fourth book of *On Meteorology* <note>original: "de Meteoris", a foundational Greek text on natural science</note>, where he says at the conclusion: that when red, pure sulfur and quicksilver come together in a semi-pure, dry earth and strike against one another, and the **Sun** <note>represented by the alchemical symbol for Gold, Sol</note> also manifests its **influence** <term>the celestial or astrological power believed to radiate from planets to earth</term> through its action, then—I say—the Sun or Gold is generated and brought forth. This happens specifically through Nature’s means of a long and steady **decoction** <term>original: "Decoction", the process of maturing or ripening through gentle, constant heat</term> that requires time and day to complete. In the same manner, it is also generated and brought forth through **sublimation** <note>original: "Überschwebung", a process where a substance is heated into vapor and then solidifies again</note>; so that the unbreakable mother of the earth reduces and brings back the sulfur and quicksilver into a common **essence** <term>the fundamental nature or "soul" of the substance</term> which is luminous, shining, and transparent. This also applies to all other unbreakable gemstones, depending on how the heat of the sulfur changes—that is, whether it is intense or slight.

<column-break/>

And when a white sulfur and quicksilver meet in a pure earth, and the **Moon** <note>original: "Luna", the alchemical planet associated with Silver</note> unites them with her influence, then silver is generated and brought forth. It has no difference from gold except for this: that with gold there is a pure sulfur, whereas for the latter <note>Silver</note>, a sulfur has arrived which has become incombustible through the influence of the heavens, moving through the <unclear>spheres</unclear> day and night. But if <margin>Burning:</margin> any kind of impure, burning sulfur comes to the quicksilver in a pure and stinking earth, when **Mars** <note>the planet associated with Iron</note> manifests his influence, then iron is generated and brought forth. But when black and impure sulfur comes to the quicksilver in the earth where **Saturn** <note>the planet associated with Lead</note> then reigns, lead is generated and brought forth. Furthermore, if a white, impure sulfur comes to the quicksilver in the earth at the hours when **Jupiter** <note>the planet associated with Tin</note> reigns, then tin is generated and brought forth. And that metal becomes unstable, for the quicksilver is not well mixed with the sulfur; anyone can easily see and understand the difference between these and gold. Therefore, Aristotle also says that lead is gold—just as one might also say that all imperfect metals are iron, and thus they are "imperfect" and "weak" gold.

All this **Saint Thomas Aquinas** <term>Sanctus Thomas de Aquino</term> <note>a prominent 13th-century theologian to whom many alchemical works were pseudonymously attributed</note> writes in the book, as was mentioned above, to the King of **Jerusalem** in his time.

### The seventh chapter on the nature and property of Lead, and on its purgation, separation, preparation, clarification, manifold conditions, and roasting or hardening.

But before we begin to describe its nature and property, we must know above all things that **Lead** is called by many and various names. # Bernard says this concerning the Hymns and Canticles,

Those who do not yet have a teacher (<term>praeceptor</term> <note>Latin for teacher or instructor</note>) and wish to listen to me, and are not ashamed to walk through the right order of life; for he who fights in spiritual matters—that is, in God’s work—and wishes to be both a <term>discipulus</term> <note>student</note> and a <term>magister</term> <note>master</note> or teacher at the same time, they are nothing else [but lost]. While they believe they can see through everything, they are so burdened that they falter; and even if they bring many students together, it is so arranged that one can say to them: "How shall one blind man show the way to another?" For experience shows that many have been led away from the right path into horrible errors, not without danger to their salvation. For such people do not understand nor know the deceit and cunning of the intellect, nor its swift presumptions. Thus it happens that those who have partially begun to live according to the Spirit and to resist evil lusts and desires are overcome by the flesh and fall into horrible errors, shame, and vice, falling grievously. Therefore, such people must be very careful to walk cautiously. For he gives his hand to the deceiver, who pretends to obey his teacher <note>original Latin: "Nam seductori dat manum, qui parere dissimulat praeceptori"</note>. That is, he who will not listen to teachers, but imagines he understands everything better himself and is clever enough, delivers himself into the hands of the deceiver and plunges into such error and conceit. Thus he says.

<meta>catchword: Item</meta>

<column-break/>

Also, in another place he says this:
An unlearned and ignorant priest or monk, and a layman (the common man) who understands a little and has some learning—imagine such people coming together and conferring with one another, discussing matters; from this, very little good will come. So says Johannes Capistranus <note>Giovanni da Capistrano (1386–1456), a famous Franciscan friar and preacher known as the "Soldier Saint."</note>.

# There follows a treatise on a stage or setting of the work

Concerning a substance in the name of the Lord the Son, which is well purified and made clean, then tested by a <term>cementum</term> <note>A "cement" in alchemy refers to a corrosive paste used to refine precious metals, usually gold, by removing impurities through heat.</note>, and according to the subtle clarity of its beauty—just as painters use for gilding—for those who love it and desire it to burn fiercely. It must first be distilled seven or nine times in a clean and strong <term>urinale</term> <note>A glass vessel shaped like a urine flask, commonly used in laboratory work.</note> or glass, using the lid with the <term>alembic</term> <note>The "beak" or "cap" of the distilling apparatus that directs the condensed vapor into a receiving vessel.</note>. And that which has been guided through is placed in a <term>phialle</term> <note>vial</note> or furnace in heat that is not too cold, but with a gentle fire. [Put] for several days into this aforementioned burning water the now-mentioned <term>Sol</term> <note>The sun symbol ☉ represents Gold.</note>, one part or grain after the other, until it is all settled within. One should know, however, that for one part of Gold, there should be only four parts of the burning water, and that the water should be renovated and renewed every time. When this has happened, close the urinal or glass with its alembic.

And first give it a gentle fire, [like] a sunburn, the longer the more, yet quite gently and slowly, so that everything is properly distilled until soft. Then take the gold powders (<term>Pulvis Solis</term> <note>original: "Pülveres solis," meaning powder of the Sun or gold</note>), which remain at the bottom of the urinal-shaped glass <note>a rounded alchemical vessel</note> or form-glass. And because they have [formed] quite dense glass-like tablets on top, put them back into the aforementioned urinal-shaped glass or form-glass a second time. And when you have poured wine or other brandy-water <note>distilled spirits or aqua vitae</note> over it, place the glass in a furnace (<term>furnellum</term> <note>original: "furnellum oder Ofen"</note>), and distill it through completely just as you did before, except for this: that it is only rubbed onto a glass tablet for the first time. And so the gold powder shall be sufficiently calcined <note>reduced to a fine powder through heat</note> into a proper and incomprehensible powder. 

Once this has happened, you must take good, pure honey, which has been well skimmed, as much as you think you need for the impastation <note>the process of kneading a powder into a thick paste</note> of the given powder. And when the aforementioned material (<term>materia</term>) is all made into a paste, place it in a glass distillation vessel and incorporate it well with a glass rod (<term>bacillus</term> <note>original: "bacilo oder stäblein"</note>), so that it becomes like marrow or an ointment. Afterward, let it stand a little while on the lukewarm ashes. Then you should have warm, sweet water in another glass vessel. And put the aforementioned material into it and let them cook (<term>coquire</term> <note>original: "coquiren oder sieden"</note>) or boil together well; afterward, let the material settle overnight. And then

distill it through a filter (<term>filtrum</term>), so that the oil or water settles at the bottom. Afterward, coagulate <note>thicken or solidify</note> the aforementioned material and let it dry out. Likewise, take that same aforementioned gold powder and add more of the above-described honey to it in all things, just as you did before. Do this a third time. And at that time, the parts of the half-portion shall be well calcined and prepared so that they can resolve themselves into the First Matter (<term>Prima Materia</term> <note>the fundamental primitive substance from which all matter was thought to originate</note>) and into a water. 

For all minerals, and especially the metals (<term>metalla</term>), are made from water, as can be clearly seen from this: that they are converted and transformed into water like other composite or joined bodies (<term>corpora</term>). The solution <note>the dissolving into liquid</note> of this aforementioned powder is always accomplished thus: Take the same prepared water, then take newly laid chicken eggs that have been well cooked and hardened, and cut them in half, and remove the egg yolks. And take the aforementioned egg whites (<term>albumina</term> <note>original: "Albumina oder Eyer weiß"</note>), then you must have two wide glass bowls, and in such bowls, place and arrange the aforementioned egg whites (<term>albumen ovorum</term>) into the concentrated or hollow vessels so that you make a solar arrangement (<term>solarium</term> <note>likely a specific arrangement of vessels to catch "solar" influence or simply for evaporation</note>).

### Another water, etc.

Another water for the distillation of living mercury <term>Mercury</term> <note>Commonly known today as quicksilver</note>; with this, everything shall be prepared. Take 1/2 pound of Roman Vitriol <term>Vitrioll</term> <note>Usually copper or iron sulfate</note>, 2 pounds of saltpeter <term>salis petrae</term>, and 4 ounces of sal ammoniac <term>salis Armoniaci</term> <note>Ammonium chloride, used as a flux or to create strong acids</note>. Each of these should be made into a fine powder individually. From this powder, create a water <note>This refers to creating a strong mineral acid, likely a form of aqua regia or nitric acid, through distillation</note>. Use it in all things exactly as was taught and understood in the preceding process. Afterward, take this water that has been made and place into it 1 ounce of raw, living mercury. At this time, it should be mixed and dedicated or given over to the solution <note>The process of dissolving a solid into a liquid</note>. Let it be patiently refined into a water; and if it does not wish to dissolve quickly, then place the flasks <term>Ampullen</term> in which you have placed it, along with the water in which it is meant to be dissolved, into a hood-full of ashes or upon the ashes, as was said and mentioned above. Make a gentle fire beneath it until the water in the mentioned flask is dissolved.

### A Strong Water or Parting-Water

Take one pound of **saltpeter** <note>original: *salis Nitri*; potassium nitrate</note>, and add to it one pound of **vitriol** <note>original: *Vitrioli*; metal sulfates</note>. And thus take two pounds of saltpeter and two pounds of vitriol together and mixed with one another, until the composition reaches twenty or thirty **weights** <note>original: *pondera*; a general unit of weight, likely pounds in this context</note>. And when it is ready, place each batch of the composition into a separate **flask** <note>original: *Amphoram*; a large vessel for liquids</note> or gourd, and set the **helmets** <note>original: *Helmen*; the top part of a still, also called an alembic</note> upon them. Then place them on or in the furnaces and surround them neatly with earth <note>This refers to a sand-bath or "pelican" setup where vessels are nestled in earth or sand to distribute heat evenly and prevent the glass from cracking</note>. Give them at first a gentle fire until the matter in the flasks begins to **dissolve** <note>original: *dissolvirn*</note>. And if you notice that the matter in the **solution** <note>original: *Solution*</note> wants to rise up or overflow, then remove some of the fire and manage it with a

<column-break/>

gentle or moderate fire until the matter in the flasks has settled and subsided. Note also that the flasks should stand in the earth up to the third part [one-third deep], but the upper and unbent part should extend out above the earth. When the **vapors** <note>original: *Spiritus*; "spirits" or volatile gases released during heating</note> begin to turn bluish, the fire should be increased, and these same vessels should be **sealed** <note>original: *Verlutet*; "luted," or sealed with a paste made of clay, dung, or lime to make the joints airtight</note> with good **mastery** <note>original: *magisterij*</note>. The vessels, however, must be filled with earth all the way to the top, and this great fire must be held steady until the **alembic** <note>original: *Alembicus*; the distillation head</note> above becomes finely **whitened** <note>original: *dealbirt*</note> and white. Note also, when the **receivers** <note>original: *recipientia*; the vessels that catch the distilled liquid</note> are sealed, that you should leave a small hole in each receiver so that the vessel does not break or burst. And if it should happen that the matter, because of too great a heat, wants to run out, then take a small cloth, dip it into cold water, wring it out, and—keeping it quite wet so that the glass does not burst—wrap it neatly around the glass; thus the excess heat will subside and be stilled.

## Item: How one should make a cupel or crucible shard

Take 2 parts of sifted ashes and 1 part of finely ground sand. Mix them thoroughly with one another and moisten or sprinkle them with water—not too damp, but just so the matter becomes wet enough that a round ball can be made of it by hand. And after proper preparation, place the matter into a **test** <note>original: *Testam*; a shallow vessel used in refining</note> or the shard of a barrel; compress it all together with your thumb and hollow it out with a small, curved knife that is bent at the front, however you like it. And press it firmly with a bright or smooth stone so that the ashes remain full and dense together. And let them dry out in this manner.

# An **Aqua Fortis** or **Separating Water** that **separates gold or silver**, and how all is made /

Take 3 parts **Saltpeter** <note>original: *Salis Nitri*</note>, 1 part **Alum** <note>original: *Aluns*</note>, and $\frac{1}{2}$ part **Vitriol** <note>original: *Vitrioli*; likely copper or iron sulfate</note>, and a handful of **unslaked lime** <note>original: *ungelöschtes kalcks*</note>. Grind them into a powder and mix well together in wine or spring water. Place them in a **cucurbit** <note>original: *Cucurbitam*; a gourd-shaped chemical flask</note> or **flask** <note>original: *kolben*</note> and let them stand still for three days.

Take beaten or **leaf gold** <note>original: *Blättlin Goldt*</note> and rub it upon a stone. Add **Aqua Regia** <note>original: *Aqua-regis*; "Royal Water," a mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acids capable of dissolving gold</note> to it, and the gold will **dissolve** <note>original: *dissoluiren*</note>. When this has happened, add **Sal ammoniac** <note>original: *Salmiac*</note> to it, and the **mercury** <note>original: *Mercurius*</note> will be consumed and used up. Afterward, wash it in **shells** <note>original: *Conchis, Muscheln oder schalen*; this refers to the creation of "shell gold" used by illuminators</note> or bowls until it becomes pure. After that, rub it upon a stone again. Finally, make a liquid with **gum tragacanth** <note>original: *tragantischem Gummi*; a natural binder</note>, using as much as there was gold previously, and mix or stir it together. Use this for whatever you wish to write, and afterward polish the writing with a **wild boar’s tooth** <note>a traditional tool for burnishing gold to a high shine</note>.

# On Weights and Measures

->Isidore writes thus /<-

> It is helpful to know the manner of weights and measures. <note>original Latin: *Ponderum ac mensurarum iuvat cognoscere modum.*</note>

Now we also wish to recognize the names of the weights and **measures** <note>original: *mensurarum*</note> and to have them, understanding what and how much each holds or contains and signifies. For all things that have a **body** <note>original: *Corpus*</note>, from the highest to the lowest—as it is written—are disposed and shaped together according to **quantity** <note>original: *Menge*</note> or **measure** <note>original: *Maaß*</note>, or according to **number**, or according to **weight**. For **Nature**, which governs all things, has given each physical thing its own weight. This is seen in **Moses**—who is older than all heathen philosophers—who in many and various places of the **Holy Scriptures** established the distinction of **times, numbers, measures, and weights**,

<margin>*</margin>
And of schools, both learned and unlearned, he is the first who has written and taught the distinction of weights so **exquisitely** <note>original: *exquisiti*</note> and correctly. For although many other authors are found who have written of this, there is yet none who has been more experienced in this art, and none who has come as close to us in what pertains to this **treatise** <note>original: *Tractatum*</note> as the author and writer just described.

<meta>This page continues the technical and medicinal discussion, transitioning from chemical preparations to a philosophical and practical overview of weights and measures. It defines the terminology used in weighing, moving from Latin etymology to the specific types of scales used in commerce and the smallest units of measurement like the siliqua.</meta>

**Weight** <note>original: *pondus*</note> A weight or pound takes its name from the fact that it hangs <note>Latin: *pendere*</note> when it is weighed by means of the **tongue** <note>the needle or indicator on a scale</note>. For this reason, it is also called an **expense** <note>original: *Epensum*; meaning something weighed out</note>, because it is not properly named except when it is being weighed or hung up for weighing.

**Weight** <note>original: *Pondus*</note> also takes on a specific meaning, which is as much as **one pound** <note>original: *libra vna*</note>, although this is not strictly accurate, but rather a common usage. From this also comes the word **Dipondius**, which means **two-pounder**, as if one were to say "having two weights" <note>original: *Duo pondera habens*</note>. This term *Dipondius*, for something weighing two pounds, is still common and in use in the Latin language today.

**Balance scale** <note>original: *Trutina* or *Kiepstuhlwaage*</note> These are the two pans or dishes that hang opposite each other in equilibrium, so that the tongue stands exactly in the middle of them. This is also to be understood as a large scale with all its accessories, which must be hung up in a warehouse due to the heavy weights, such as hundredweights and **talents** <note>original: *Talenta*; an ancient unit of mass</note>, as one is accustomed to finding in the **Customs House** <note>original: *Zöllhauis*</note> or the **Silk-Weighing House** <note>original: *Seidwagenuis*</note>. **Moments** <note>original: *Momenta*</note>: here this little word means a small amount, a tiny and little movement of the balance beam. From this comes the word **Money** <note>original: *Moneta*</note>, which is so commonly used for **coinage** <note>original: *Müntze*</note>.

**Steelyard** <note>original: *Statera*; a scale with a sliding weight on a lever arm</note> A quick-scale; this word has its name from the instrument, so that it just

---

<page-num>464</page-num>

it just stands level <note>original: *gleich inen stehet*</note> when it is hung or pulled up with the **zinc trigger** <note>original: *Zinc wegdrückel*; likely a metal release or mechanism</note> and the tongue or **stylus** in the middle.

**Capana** is a foreign or Italian word; it is the type of scale used by those living in Italy or the Latin lands. This type of scale does not have two dishes like the others, but has only one **platform** <note>original: *Schiffm*</note> or frame, which is marked according to the pounds and ounces or **lots** <note>a *Loth* was a traditional Germanic unit of weight, about 1/32nd of a pound</note>, and one weighs upon it according to various weights.

**Examination** <note>original: *Examen*</note> This refers to the nature of the **tongue** <note>the indicator needle</note>, according to which one must primarily guide oneself during weighing.

However, one must give every weight a certain measure and name, so that it may be named properly and correctly.

**Chalcis** is the smallest part of a weight based on the pound; it is the fourth part of an **obolus** <note>a small Greek coin/weight</note>, or half [a weight], containing 2 grains. But all together it is *Chalcis*, which is the most precious and is, as it were, the beginning of weight; just as a **pebble** <note>original: *Calculis*</note> is a small indicator, not a pound in weight, but a beginning; although it is so small that one may and can step upon it without feeling any discomfort.

**Siliqua** is the 24th part of a **solidus** <note>a late Roman gold coin</note> or a whole; it has its name from the tree <note>the Carob tree</note>, specifically from its seed. <margin>A *Siliqua* is a seed of the tree; it is for us a half-scruple, which is half a *Loth*...</margin>

**Ceratius** <note>original: *Ceratius*; the origin of the word "carat"</note> is the same part of an obolus, [namely] half, which is a *siliqua*. Therefore the Latins called it a **half-obolus** <note>original: *Semiobulum*</note>. In Greek it is *Ceratium*, but in Latin the *siliqua* is weighed as three [grains], having...

The **Solidus** is called by another name, the **Sextula**, by the Latins, for it is completed as a sixth part <note>original: *sextuors*</note> of twelve **ounces** <note>original: *Unzen*</note>. For as we have said, the common people call it the **Golden Solidus** <note>original: *aureum solidum*</note>: a third part of which they called a **Tremissis**, because it constitutes <insert>a portion of</insert> the solidus. A **Tremissis**, when the **Sextula** is taken twice, makes a **Duellum** <note>a Roman weight equal to two sextulae, or 1/36 of a pound</note>, and when taken three times, it returns a **Stater**.

The **Stater**, however, is half of an **Ounce** <note>original: *Unciae*</note>, weighing three gold pieces. From this, it is called a *Stater*, because it "stands" <note>Latin: *stare*</note> for three solidi. From this also comes the **Semi-ounce** <note>original: *semiuncia*</note>, because it is half of an ounce. This is also called a **Semissis** since it is half of the weight, just as a *semis* is half of an **As** <note>a Roman unit of weight or currency</note>.

The Hebrews similarly call the **Quadrant** <note>original: *Quadrantem*</note> a quadrant; and it is called a **Quadrans** because it weighs a fourth part of an ounce. The **Sicol**, which is corruptly called a *Siclus* in the Latin language, is a Hebrew name, having among them the weight of an ounce. A **Sicel** or **Shekel** <note>original: *Seckel*</note> is a Hebrew word; among the Hebrews, it contains as much as one ounce <note>original: *j. ℥.*</note> among us.

Among the Latins, however, this is a fourth part and half of a stater, weighing two **drachmas** <note>original: *Dragmas*</note>. Among the Latins and Greeks, it is the fourth part of an ounce and half a stater, approximately two **Quintlein** <note>a small German unit of weight, 1/4 of a Lot</note>, which is half a **Lot** <note>a historical German unit of weight, roughly 15-16 grams</note>.

When one reads of this same unit in the **Holy Scripture** as a *Sichlis* or **Shekel**, one should understand that it means as much as one ounce or two **Lots** in our system. However, when one reads this little word elsewhere in **Pagan writings** <note>original: *Heÿdnischen Schrifften*; referring to non-Biblical Greek or Roman classical texts</note>, it should...

If one gives it to someone to eat, it brings about death because of its **poison** <note>original Latin: *Venini*</note>. <meta>This page continues the technical alchemical instructions from the previous page, moving from the creation of "sulfur" to the preparation of various salts and the transmutation of copper into silver, as well as the augmentation of gold. Item: **Sal Ammoniac** <note>original: *das Armoniacus*, ammonium chloride</note> is prepared in exactly the same way as common salt, but not three times. In the same manner, **alum** <note>original: *Salauñ*</note>, or **sheet alum** <note>original: *Alumen lamenis*</note>, or **selenite** <note>original: *Spatglas*, a translucent variety of gypsum</note> are all prepared. Take sublimated sheet alum and place it in a glass vessel and set it over a gentle fire; then it melts like wax. But let it remain on the fire so that all its **moisture** <note>original: *Humiditas*</note> flows out and passes away, and it becomes very hard. Afterward, grind it and put it into cold water; **distill** <note>in this context, likely meaning to strain or drip</note> it through a **filter** <note>original: *Filtrum*</note> and finally **coagulate** it. Thus it is correct and prepared and refined for all **baths** <note>original: *bagn*, referring to chemical baths or procedures</note>.

Item: Take three **loths** <note>a unit of weight, roughly 15 grams</note> of raw **mercury** <note>symbolized by ☿</note> and one **loth** of **salt** <note>original: *Salcke*, likely a transcription error for *Salze*</note>. When they have been made into a powder together and a subtle powder has been produced, then combine them with one another. Then place them in a vessel of your choosing and let them **descend** <note>a form of distillation where the vapor is forced downward</note> through a **bearded pot** <note>original: *Botum Barbatum*, a specialized distillation vessel</note>. For the **arsenic** <note>original: *Arsenicus*</note> will descend or sink down everywhere like an earthy substance. One part of this arsenic, unified and processed, transforms 10 parts of the fullness of **Venus** <note>original: *Veneris*, alchemical code for copper</note> into good **Moon** <note>original: *Lunam*, alchemical code for silver</note>.

Item: When you wish to **rubify** <note>original: *rubificirn*, to turn red</note> the mercury or make it red, place yellow ground **sulfur** <note>original: *Sulphur*</note> above and below it in a <term>dreyellen</term> <note>a tall, three-legged vessel or a specific long-necked flask</note>

<insert>in a dreyellen</insert>

<column-break/>

in a **three-legged vessel** <note>original: *dreyellen*</note>, and take good care that you do not close the top of the vessel at the **opening** <note>original: *Orificio*</note> or exit. Set it over a gentle fire, for the sulfur will decrease and become less, but the **mercury** <note>original: *Mercurius*</note> will become entirely red from it and also remain red.

Item: **Minium** <note>original: *Menium*, red lead</note> and **alkali salt** <note>original: *Sal Alkali*</note> are made from two parts of quicklime and one part of wood ash. Item: **Salt of Tartar** <note>original: *Sal Tartari*, potassium carbonate</note> is made from burnt **tartar** <note>original: *Tartaro* or *Weinstein*, the sediment from wine barrels</note> and warm water. Take **nitre** <note>original: *Nitri*, saltpeter</note> and **glass gall** <note>original: *Fel Vitri*, the scum found on molten glass</note>; **do this by itself** <note>original: *fac per se*</note>.

Furthermore, you should note well that **Sun** <note>original: *Sol*, alchemical code for gold</note> and **Moon** <note>original: *Luna*, alchemical code for silver</note> can all be separated and augmented or diminished. Take **gold** <note>original: *Solem*</note>, **copper** <note>original: *Venerem*</note>, and **red sulfur**, in **equal parts** <note>original: *Ana*</note>. Melt the first two species in a **crucible** <note>original: *Crucibulo*</note>. When they are melted, put the sulfur into it and mix them well together with a wooden stick that has a small hook for holding; this [vessel] should have a hole at the bottom, and draw the matter into it. When it has become cold, take the matter and divide it, and you will find that the **gold** <note>original: *sol*</note> has been slightly **augmented** and increased among the lesser metals. Repeat this preliminary work or labor in all parts exactly as before, thirty-three times.

### Oil of Saturn is made thus

Take lead ashes, rubbed as well as you wish, place them in a glazed <term>pot</term> <note>original: "Hafen"</note> or glass, and pour wine vinegar over them so that it stands three fingers high or more over them. Seal it well at the top and set it in the sun or in the sand for one day or longer. Give it a moderate fire so that the material boils without ceasing. Stir it occasionally with a spatula and seal it up again. Afterward, lift it from the fire and stir it well. After this, let it become pure or clear. Then strain it off into a glass, seal it, and take heed: this is called the <term>Oil of Saturn</term>, made from lead ashes.

<meta>This page continues the introduction to the work 'On Essences' (De essentijs), specifically addressing the origins and composition of mineral and animal stones, drawing on the theories of Aristotle and Avicenna.</meta>

...must [be], that the elements and heavenly circles of the Matter, out of which they are composed and disposed, are infused or generated by means of many forms and **Actions** <note>original: "Actionibus"</note> or effects. The Matter <note>original: "Materia"</note> of the stone, however, is a coarse and thick water, which carries many earthy substances with it, or perhaps only a few, depending on whether the stone is clear and bright or dark. 

In this way **Aristotle** seeks the ultimate cause, which is written in the **Meteorology** <note>original: "Meteoris"; referring to Aristotle's treatise on natural philosophy</note> (though we would rather say, as **Avicenna** has thus said and taught): that a stone is **not** generated and made from a pure earth, but rather through any earth that is full of water. However, we believe that in certain flowing waters, stones are generated and begotten. We also see that salts grow and are made from every material that has many earthy substances; but we also have [the knowledge] that stones are begotten through the heat of the sun and fire.

In the same way, the Matter of stones is a coarse and thick water, but the **Agent** <note>original: "Agens"</note>—that is, what makes and works such stones—is either heat or cold. These **agents** <note>original: "agentia"</note> congeal such water, or [bring] from their water into the veins of the causes and effects of a stone... for they are [made] through a...

<column-break/>

...both in **Plants** and also in **Animals** or creatures. You must not simply assume that these stones are placed there, but rather that they have great power and virtue, for they are congealed in them **by an internal animal virtue** <note>original Latin: "Virtute animalitatis Intrinseca"</note>—that is, by the power that these same animals possess. 

Just as the carbuncle stone <note>a glowing red gemstone, often identified as a garnet or ruby</note> is congealed and grows in the head of certain snakes, and more could be said of other precious stones; but you may certainly believe that such stones taken from certain animals are much more precious and powerful than other stones. 

Some, however, are coagulated through the power of Art in cooperation with Nature, as **Aristotle** has wisely explained regarding this: that some make a water out of stones and compose it, which they call **Virgin’s Milk** <note>original: "Lac Virginis"; a common alchemical term for various white liquid suspensions, often involving lead or antimony</note>, and coagulate that into a stone.

### of the Metals, etc.

There is, however, another and much more glorious method <term>Modus</term> or way to transform fixed arsenic <term>Arsenicum fixum</term> into gold or silver, through the power and virtue of the white sulfur <term>Sulphuris</term> (or brimstone <term>schwebels</term>), or through the power of the red sulfur <term>Sulphuris</term> which is not <unclear>corrupted</unclear>. ### Following concerning the Stone, namely the Sulfur or Sulphur.

Take 1 lb of the same in the name of the Lord and crush or break it up inside upon a marble stone, and soak <term>imbibire</term> it with 1 1/2 lbs of common oil or with 1/4 lb of linseed oil; so that it becomes just like a paste. And constantly stir the matter <term>Materiam</term> with an iron spatula, and when the matter has settled again, place the pan or

pan or the crucible back over the fire; and repeat this often until it becomes as thick as honey. Cut such sulfur into small nail-like pieces <note>original: "Negel," which could refer to nail-shaped fragments or cloves</note>. Then take an equal amount of oil of tartar <note>original: "Weingstein ölle," a potassium carbonate solution used as a solvent</note>, weighing as much as the sulfur, and place them in a pan or crucible upon the fire. Subsequently, cut this preparation <term>Confection</term> again into small nail-like pieces, and place it in a glass cucurbit <term>Cucurbitam</term> <note>the lower, gourd-shaped vessel used in distillation</note>, and place an alembic <term>Alembicum</term> <note>the lid or head of the distilling apparatus</note> upon it, and distill. # A burning water is made thus

Take an old red wine and equal parts of <term>orpiment</term> <note>original: *Auripigmenti*; a deep orange-yellow arsenic sulfide mineral used as a pigment and in alchemy</note> or arsenic, namely 1 lb. Take ½ lb of <term>sulfur of wine</term> <note>original: *Sulphuris Vini*; likely refers to a highly concentrated spirit of wine or a specific sulfurous extract</note> or "live" sulfur, and ¼ lb of unslaked lime. Place all of these into a distillation vessel specially formed and made for this purpose, and distill them just as you would a rose water. The particular virtue of this water is this: if you dip a finger into it, it appears as if it is burning, yet it does not burn the person at all. <note>original: *deß Marien nichts*; this is an unusual phrasing, possibly a corruption of "dermaßen nichts" meaning "not at all," or a specific reference to the body.</note> However, if you dip a light or a candle into it, it will not ignite, even if you submerge it deep under the water. And as was clearly stated before, this was taken <insert>from a</insert> little treatise by Saint Thomas Aquinas, which he wrote in the year 1506, and which came to me—

This is because the "multitude"—that is, the common man—is not worthy of such secrets. As I went into the <term>cave</term> <note>original: *höll*; literally "hell," but in Hermetic tradition, it refers to the hidden chamber or "vane" where Hermes is said to have been found</note>, I took an Emerald Tablet which was written by Hermes' own hand. > <note>original Latin: "Quod superius, est sicut inferius, Et quod est inferius, est sicut quod est superius ad perpetranda miracula unius rei : Sicut res omnes ab una fuerunt meditatione unius / sic etiam fuerunt res omnes abhac re una operatione."</note>
> That which is above is like that which is below, and that which is below is like that which is above, to accomplish the miracles of the One Thing. Just as all things come from the contemplation of the One, so all things are born from this one thing by a single operation and action.

Truth: That which is above is exactly like that which is at the bottom. And that which is below is exactly like that which is at the top. The miracle of the wonder-work shall join the one, just as all things come from the meditation of one alone. So too have all things arisen from this thing through its operation and effect alone. Its father is the Sun (*Sol*), its mother is the Moon (*Luna*). The wind has carried it in its body or belly. Its nurse is the Earth (*Terra*).

# A short but profound
### Treatise of the Blessed Thomas Aquinas.
### On the Highest Philosophical Stone.

Within the mine <note>original: Minera; refers to the raw mineral source or ore</note>, a red volatile spirit is found, which is called **Bilocis**, **Bile of the Gall** <note>original: Fel Bilis Gall; likely a reference to the bitter or transformative nature of the substance</note>, etc. It is the fire and origin and the father of all alums and all salts, and of all volatile and melting metals. And the first surname, that which flies out before it, is a **vapor** or steam, which is condensed and made thick in the water; it does not cling to that which it touches <note>A classic description of quicksilver (mercury), which does not "wet" surfaces</note> because something sulfurous and earthy is mixed beneath it, by which it is to some extent inspissated <term>inspissated: thickened or made dense, usually by evaporation or chemical concentration</term> and made thick. For this reason, it is also called **Sulfur Water** <note>original: Aqua sulphuris</note>, a soft water that is not mixed with any impurity. Therefore, Plato also said: <note>original: "Nisi purum Sulphuris proijciatur super multum corporis, ita ut super illud habeat potestatem conuertendi ipsium cito in pulverem, cuius color erit sicut color corporis, super quem projicitur spiritus &c."</note> "Unless a small amount of pure sulphur is cast upon much of the body, so that it has the power to convert it quickly into a powder, the color of which shall be like the color of the body upon which the spirit is cast, etc." This means that unless a small or minute part of the sulphur is measured against a large part of the body, which can overpower it, then the sulphur will not quickly transform the body into a powder whose color is the same as the color of the body through which the <term>spirit; original: spiritus</term> was infused.

## Following is the Fourth Regimen
### Which, according to the advice of the Father and Pythagoras, is Fixation

The fourth <term>regimen; original: Regimen</term> is, according to the instruction of Pythagoras, <term>fixation; original: Figiren</term> or binding. <note>original: "Quoniam argentum vivum non congelat ignis patiens."</note> "Because a patient [mild] fire does not congeal quicksilver." Likewise, the <term>oil; original: Oleum</term> is like the <term>soul; original: Seele</term>, which is withdrawn or extracted into itself only through the washing of the water, the distillation, and the application of fire. The water, however, is a <term>spirit; original: spiritus</term> which extracts and draws out the <term>souls; original: Animas</term> from the <term>bodies; original: Corporibus</term>. When the soul is extracted from the body, it remains in the spirit, which spirit is the "place" of the soul. The soul is a gentle <term>tincture; original: Tinctur</term> brought forth in the spirit, just as a dye is carried by water onto a cloth; for the water yields when the distillation or drying is forced, and the tincture remains fixed in the cloth through its oiliness. So it is also with the water in which the tincture of light is carried. When it is reduced, or when it mixes with the <term>foliated earth; original: Terram foliatum</term> in the air, the spiritual water is immediately dried, and the soul remains in the body, which is a tincture of the air. ### A Calcination of Jove or
### of Tin

Take of **Jove** <note>original: *Iouis*; the alchemical name for Jupiter, which represents the metal Tin</note> or Tin as you please, melt it, and quench it 11 times in common Salt which has been purified and cleansed with good Wine-Vinegar and with 4 <term>ounces</term> <note>the symbol ℥ denotes an ounce in apothecary weight</note> of Honey. ### make Tin entirely malleable

Take Jove or Tin as much as you want,

### A Calcination of Venus or
### of Copper

Take 1 lb. of unslaked calcined **Tartar** <note>original: *Tartari* or *Weinstein*; the potassium bitartrate crystals found in wine barrels, used as a flux</note>, and 1 lb. of common Salt. One measure of spring water; boil this until it seethes, and distill it through a filter. Lay **Venus** <note>the alchemical name for Copper</note> therein, and it will become a powder / Wash the powder two or three times with clear or pure lye; afterward, wash it also with lukewarm water three or four times, and then lay it in a glazed vessel and let it dry out over the fire.

And place it in a kettle with water over the fire, and let it soak well for 12 hours; stir it, and do not let it hinder you even though the **Medicine** <note>original: *Medicina*; here referring to the alchemical substance being prepared</note> will be hard. Afterward, place it in a **Cucurbit** <note>a gourd-shaped glass vessel used in distillation</note> or flask, and attach an **Alembic** <note>the "cap" or lid of a still that redirects vapors</note>, and seal the glass well with **Lute of Wisdom** <note>original: *Lute sapientiae*; a specialized airtight clay or paste used to seal alchemical apparatus</note>. Give it first a gentle fire until the white water is distilled. Afterward, when the **Alembic** begins to turn bluish, then take away the white water and take the other, and let everything proceed through the **Alembic** until that which stands in the way comes down again.

Afterward, divide this second water into three parts, and divide one of those parts again into three parts. Of such a divided [portion], take 4 <term>Loth</term> <note>a historical German unit of weight, roughly equivalent to half an ounce or 15 grams</note> of purified **Mercury**, and lay it in a small bowl or dish, and pour upon such **Mercury** the first part of the divided water from the last **division** or partition, and it **dissolves** <note>original: *solvirts*</note> it immediately.

Afterward, take 4 <term>Loth</term> of **Silver** <note>original: *Argenti vivi*, which literally means "living silver" or mercury, but the text specifies it is "well-filed," implying solid silver metal</note> which is well-filed or has been cut in <term>parting-water</term> <note>nitric acid used to separate metals</note>, and pour upon it the second part of the water from the last **division**, and the silver also **dissolves** immediately. If it will not immediately **dissolve** in a dish, then you can first give it assistance in a <term>cupel</term> <note>a shallow porous dish used in assaying</note>, and everything will **dissolve** better. Press

<column-break/>

it well, however, so that the glass does not crack, now and then, in which the **Mercury** now is. After this, pour the three waters into a dish and mix them with a bone stirrer and **coagulate** <note>to thicken or solidify a liquid</note> them. And when it has been **coagulated**, then dissolve it again with the water of the first **division** or partition, and **coagulate** it, and then do the same thing again; and do this three or four times, and the oil will become so subtle.

Take 1 **part** <note>original: *partem*</note> of this same oil and a 100-fold amount of **Mercury**, and lay them in a dish, very painstakingly; then set the dish in a **Philosophical Oven** <note>an alchemical furnace designed to maintain a constant, steady heat over long periods</note>, and let it stand for 8 days or a little longer; everything will become a powder from it.

Of this same powder, take 1 <term>Loth</term>, and 100 <term>Loth</term> of purified **Mercury**, and first lay the **Mercury** in a crucible, and as it begins to smoke, then pour the aforementioned powder into it! **And let it go anew** <note>original Latin: *Et mitte recenter ire*</note> and let it proceed once more, so you shall obtain a good **Gain** <note>original: *Lucrum*; referring to the successful transmutation into precious metal</note>, which comes from all **fusions**, that is, meltings, or from Tin. Do this so they may hardly come to help [themselves] with it, for God’s sake. (P. C) <note>These initials may refer to the author or a closing prayer formula like *Pauperibus Christi*, "for Christ's poor"</note>

<meta>This page continues the specific chemical procedures for creating an alchemical "Medicine." The previous page established the initial preparation of silver and mercury using distilled "waters." This page details the sublimation of these substances and their eventual "conjunction" to create a salt and oil capable of transmuting base metals like copper and antimony into silver.</meta>

# A Perfect Work of Mercury
->raw Mercury in a glass of pure water.<-

Take <unclear>of the</unclear> Roman Vitriol <note>copper or iron sulfate</note>, half a pound of saltpeter <note>potassium nitrate</note>, and 3 ounces of cinnabar <note>mercury sulfide</note>. Therefore, make these into a powder, then place the powder in a very strong vessel, and **sublime** the **Mercury** <note>original: *rj*, a shorthand for Mercury</note> with its receiver. Finally, make a gentle fire beneath it until the vessel begins to turn red at the top; then seal the mouth of the flask <note>original: *tunc luta os Botie*</note>. At that time, seal the **helm** <note>the cap of the distilling vessel</note> with lute <note>airtight sealant</note>, and increase the fire moderately until nothing more drips down. Afterward, take this water and dissolve in it 1 ounce of **quicksilver** <note>original: *Argenti vivi*</note>. Then separate it cleanly through a sieve at the opening, and put it through a **cupel** <note>a shallow, porous ceramic bowl used in assaying</note>, and it will be dissolved. Keep this water and pay close attention to your work.

# How This Medicine Should Be Joined
Take 1 pound of Roman Vitriol, half a pound of saltpeter, and 3 ounces of **vermilion** or cinnabar. Make a water as before; afterward, place 3 ounces of Mercury into such water and dissolve it. Then mix them together—both the previous **Silver-water** <note>original: *Aquam Argenti*</note> and this **Mercury-water** <note>original: *Aquam Mercurij*</note>—and make a conjunction or union with its nourishment. Previously, set the same material in the earth <note>likely a sand-bath</note> through a crucible in an open furnace, and make a moderate

<column-break/>

moderate fire beneath it until that part of the water is consumed and becomes dry; afterward, let it cool. After this, place the marked vials in a glass enclosure where no sun can reach, and where the vials can be influenced by little or no light. Then, toward daybreak, they will shine like daylight, which glow is extinguished by the sun; for the frost coagulates and forces them together. These same stones are just as white and bright as a crystal and can be melted or cast, just as all the **sayings of the philosophers** <note>original: *Dicta Philosophorum*; referring to established alchemical authorities</note> or their unions testify, as they always say:
> It descends into the earth, and again children are born who do not depart similar to their fathers or parents; and it will produce a fusible salt and an incombustible oil. <note>original Latin: *Descendit in Terram, & iterum generati sunt filij non exeuntes similes patribus seu parentibus, et efficiet sal fusibile et oleum in combustibile.*</note>

It descends—or better, they descend—through the earth, and they have sired children again, who are not exactly like them, and a salt will come from it that can be melted, and an oil that does not burn. Therefore, praise God.
> If you touch copper <note>original: *latonem*</note> with this water, it is immediately whitened like silver. <note>original Latin: *Si de ista aqua tetigeris as latonem statim dealbatur ut argentum*</note>

If you touch copper or **antimony** <note>original: *Spießglantz*</note> with this water, they will immediately be transformed into silver. And see that you [...]

Concerning this, the Philosopher also says: *We find the stones that fire neither destroys nor corrupts* <note>original Latin: *Inveniamus lapides, quos ignis non destruit nec corrumpat.*</note>. He teaches the same: that such stones are certain and discovered which fire can neither consume nor spoil. Its first power and virtue is: if you should cast 1 pound <note>represented by the symbol ℔</note> or 2 Loth <note>a historical German unit of weight, approximately 1/2 ounce</note> of this stone upon 70 ounces or 140 Loth of raw **Mercury**, it transforms that same **Mercury** in one hour into the most perfect **Silver**, which can withstand all tests or fires. Its second power and virtue is this: that it is soon **distilled** <term>distillation|the process of purifying a liquid by heating and cooling</term> in the manure into a water. Of which water it is said that not only iron, but also all other metals can be silvered with it. Its third power and virtue, which is called the most glorious and greatest authority, is this:

> That concerning the aforesaid stone thus composed of the elements as stated above—namely, in Earth, sand, water, and air acting upon the said stones—if you place one [part] of this stone upon 70 [parts] of mercury as previously stated, provided that the said water is warm, 70 stones will be created from it, all possessing such great virtues. <note>original Latin: *Quod de lapide prædicto sic Elementato ut supra dictum est, scilicet in Terra arena aqua et aere facientes super dictos lapides, si posueris hunc lapidem unum super 70 mercurij ut prius dictum est, duntamen quod dicta aqua sit calida, creabuntur inde 70 Lapides omnes facientes supra tantas Virtutes.*</note>
